stages.qualification: Completed at the one authenticated seed/root pair as the first re-solve stage. C7 holds every accepted operator fixed -- the C4 public photon channel, C5 QP-side kernels, and C6 phonon-side balance with the Kaplan S_+ correction -- and replaces only the author's explicit-inverse Newton driver with qpsim's public coupled_newton_solve (fixed gap, analytic cross-Jacobian, author-intent max_iter=10 and step_rtol=1e-7). The solve starts from the identical captured author per-point thermal initial state bound by the accepted C0 evidence (the author program constructs each sweep point independently from a thermal initializer; an earlier description of this seed as a continuation state was incorrect and is corrected here) and converges at the minimal public iteration cap of 4, the same count as the author control. The solver's residual assembly evaluated at the frozen C6 state matches the accepted C6 hybrid residuals to 1.3227587648e-13 (QP) and 1.6878314118e-16 (phonon) symmetric relative L1, binding the one-component claim. At the returned root the L1 balance ratios are 3.7094353580e-14 (QP) and 5.7565249895e-12 (phonon) against the 1e-7 certificate. Under the accepted author-sampling observable the re-solved ordinate is 0.14542377851441587 versus the author control 0.12090908988993258 (the frozen author root reproduces the control exactly); under the C3-documented center-carrier interpretation the same root reads 0.07767766591390296, adjacent to the historical promoted qpsim value 0.08967258. This one-point attribution identifies the observable sampling semantics as the dominant driver of the historical qpsim-versus-author discrepancy, with the center pair-frequency label raising and the Kaplan correction slightly lowering the author-sampled ordinate. C7 claims no 300-point curve, no paper parity, and no author-equivalence of the changed iteration policy.
